headline: BTC slips to $83.7k at range lows as Bitget loss is revised up to $387.5M
summary: At 17:53 UTC on 25 September BTC is $83,689.90 against an $84,380.00 open (-0.82%), sitting only 25% up an $83,163.60-$85,247.40 band, while ETH is $2,680.91 (-0.23%, also at 25% of its $2,660.01-$2,742.42 range) and SOL is $120.60 (+3.06%), near the top of its $115.85-$122.20 range and still +8.2% on the week against +3.6% for BTC and +3.3% for ETH. The single acute story got worse, not better: Bitget raised its breach estimate from $351.6m to $387.5m after adding Zcash and TRON transfers, withdrawals are still frozen, and the exchange now says it will only publish a resumption plan by 04:00 UTC on 26 September - though Circle and Tether have frozen attacker wallets, a 5% recovery bounty is live, and the loss remains inside a User Protection Fund holding over $464m. Macro is the real weight: the 10-year Treasury yield eased about 5bp to 5.16% on reports of a phased US-Iran deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz (WTI -3% to $91.74, gold up ~1% above $4,300), but a 58.4 flash September PMI has left roughly 65-70% odds on an October Fed hike, so the level of real yields is unresolved. Positioning has kept getting lighter through all of it - Hyperliquid open interest is down to $3.29bn on BTC, $2.96bn on ETH and $735m on SOL, funding is flat at 0.00125%/h across all three, and the BTC and ETH futures premiums have flipped negative at -0.022% and -0.011% after Friday's record options expiry cleared. Fear & Greed is 71 and the composite reads 61.1, both Greed, on 354 items in 24 hours: this is a de-levered tape drifting to the low end of its range on a macro cause, with one custody story still open.

BTC.note: $83,689.90, down 0.82% and 2.4% off the $85,247.40 high, pinned at the bottom quarter of an $83,163.60-$85,247.40 band with open interest down to $3.29bn from $3.39bn four hours ago and the futures premium now negative at -0.022% - spot is trading above futures, so the marginal seller is leverage leaving, not spot distribution.

ETH.note: $2,680.91, down 0.23% and at 25% of a $2,660.01-$2,742.42 range after failing at $2,742; the premium that was the richest of the three this morning (+0.084%) has flipped to -0.011% with open interest at $2.96bn, so the speculative lean that was there at midday has been taken out.

SOL.note: $120.60, up 3.06% and 75% up its $115.85-$122.20 range, the week's leader at +8.2% and part of a broad large-alt rotation (QNT +38%, ONDO +28%, LINK +11%) on the thinnest book at $735m of open interest with a flat 0.0% premium - most reflexive of the three in both directions, and it carries the 28 September Alpenglow activation.

drivers.title: Bitget raises breach loss to $387.5m; withdrawals still frozen, plan now due 04:00 UTC 26 September
drivers.detail: Bitget revised its 24 September breach estimate up from $351.6m to $387.5m after a fuller accounting added affected Zcash and TRON transfers; the haul includes roughly 103 million XRP worth about $157m. Attackers compromised a backend wallet system and spoofed transfer data so Bitget's own authorization process approved the payouts, rather than stealing private keys, and the CEO cites IP and on-chain patterns matching North Korean state-linked activity. Withdrawals remain suspended while deposits and trading run; the exchange has launched a 5% recovery bounty, Circle and Tether have frozen attacker wallets, and the loss still sits inside a User Protection Fund holding more than $464m. The negative is the slippage in both the number and the timetable - a resumption plan is now only promised by 04:00 UTC on 26 September, which keeps a custody question open over the weekend.

drivers.title: Real yields still set the price: 10-year at 5.16% with ~65-70% odds on an October Fed hike
drivers.detail: The US 10-year Treasury yield eased roughly 5bp to 5.16% today after a two-session surge that took it to its highest level since 2007 and pulled BTC from about $87,200 to $83,500 on 23-24 September. The pause has not changed the level or the direction of travel: the preliminary September S&P Global composite PMI printed 58.4, the fastest expansion since 2021, and market-implied odds of a 25bp Fed hike in October sit around 65-70% after Governor Michael Barr's comments and a hot inflation reading. This is the channel that produced this week's drawdown, and it is the one thing that can turn today's drift into a real break of $83,163.

drivers.title: US-Iran talks enter a technical phase on a phased Strait of Hormuz reopening
drivers.detail: US and Iranian negotiators meeting on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, with Qatari mediation, have moved past initial contacts into a technical phase on a phased deal that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for Washington easing its port blockade; Tehran has floated a seven-day reopening plan and is pushing for a result before the US midterms. Markets took it straight to the energy and rates complex today: WTI fell about 3% to $91.74, Brent about 1% to roughly $105, gold rose nearly 1% above $4,300 and the 10-year eased. This is the largest single source of potential relief on the macro board, and the reason the bond selloff paused rather than extended.

drivers.title: Leverage keeps draining: open interest lower again, BTC and ETH premiums now negative
drivers.detail: Hyperliquid open interest has fallen to $3.29bn on BTC, $2.96bn on ETH and $735m on SOL, extending the decline from $4.02bn, $3.18bn and $746m on 22 September, with funding flat at 0.00125%/h on all three. More telling is the basis: the BTC and ETH futures premiums have gone negative at -0.022% and -0.011%, from +0.019% and +0.084% at midday, and SOL's sits at 0.0% - spot is trading above futures on the two majors. This follows Friday's 08:00 UTC expiry of roughly $15.6bn of Deribit options, the largest of the year, which cleared without a break, and the 24 September cascade in which about $237m of longs were liquidated in a single hour. The tape entering the weekend is less crowded than it was before the drawdown, which is the condition under which dips have historically been shallow.

drivers.title: Spot bitcoin ETFs turn 2026 net positive after a six-day, $2.8bn streak
drivers.detail: US spot bitcoin ETFs have now taken inflows for six consecutive sessions worth about $2.8bn - $999m on Monday 22 September, $714.75m Tuesday, $347m Wednesday and $191m Thursday, with BlackRock's IBIT alone at $162.63m on the final day. That streak has flipped the 2026 year-to-date figure positive to roughly $800m after a year that had been in outflow. The fall from $999m to $191m is an 81% decay in daily pace, so the bid is fading at the margin - but regulated money kept adding on the exact sessions when the 10-year hit 2007 highs, which argues the recent weakness was leverage unwinding rather than spot distribution.

drivers.title: Money rotates out of BTC into large alts while bitcoin stalls
drivers.detail: With BTC stuck under $85,000 all week, the bid has gone sideways into established large caps rather than out of the market: SOL is +3.06% today and +8.2% on the week, XRP +1.8% to about $1.56, QNT +38%, ONDO +28% and LINK +11%. On the corporate side Strategy filed an 8-K at 16:03 UTC proposing daily accrual of preferred dividends to pull STRC back toward $100, Sequans completed its bitcoin treasury exit by selling its last 314 BTC, and Tether said it has minimal exposure to EQIBank after an $89m US asset seizure. Rotation into alts while BTC dominance slips is a risk-on tell inside crypto, but it also means SOL is carrying the most positioning risk into the 28 September Alpenglow activation.

watch.what: Bitget's deadline to publish a withdrawal resumption plan. This slipped once already today and the loss estimate rose 10% with it. A clean reopening closes the story; a second delay, into a weekend with thin books, is the one item on this board that could turn a covered hack into a confidence event across exchange balances.

US-Iran technical talks in New York on a phased Strait of Hormuz reopening, with Qatari mediation and a Tehran proposal for a seven-day timetable. A deal is the cleanest path to lower oil and lower yields; a collapse puts the 10-year back at its 2007 highs and BTC back under $83,000.

Solana's Alpenglow mainnet activation (Agave 4.3): Votor replaces TowerBFT, targeting ~150ms finality versus ~12.8s and raising the unresponsive-stake tolerance to 40%. The largest protocol change of the quarter, on the thinnest book of the three at $735m of open interest.
US Consumer Confidence. Secondary on its own, but it feeds the same real-yield and October-hike channel that drove this week's drawdown.

BEA Personal Income and Outlays with the August PCE print, on quarter-end when flows get pulled around. With October hike odds near 65-70% after a 58.4 flash PMI, a hot core print prices the hike closer to certain and is the most direct scheduled risk to dip-buying next week.
September employment report (Employment Situation, 8:30 a.m. ET). First-Friday payrolls into a Fed that markets already expect to hike in October; September CPI follows on 14 October.

Context for any pullback, from the stored history: BTC has had 28 sharp dips, with +1.5% recovered within 14 days in 92.9% of cases (median 5.0 h, 78.6% within 24 h) and a typical extra drop after the trigger of -0.5%; ETH 91 dips at 92.3% (median 5.0 h) and SOL 132 dips at 93.9% (median 3.5 h). Dips during greed recovered 7 of 7 for BTC, 92.9% of 28 for ETH and 93.8% of 48 for SOL. Today's market state most resembles 2025-07-11, 2025-10-04 and 2024-07-21, after which BTC's median 30-day move was 8.0% (up in 60.0% of them). The one precursor to respect: 'Donald Trump (Truth Social) + inflation/CPI' preceded a BTC dip within 6h 2.6% of the time versus 1.0% by chance (2.72x lift, n=115).
